extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO OED/staff
extracted.subtask_description: Interim suspension and procedural directives under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 in a USPTO disciplinary matter, including grounds for suspension, required responses, referral to an ALJ, and consequences during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be ordered where proof shows the practitioner was convicted of a serious crime; here the request for interim suspension was predicated on proof that Respondent was convicted of a serious crime, namely Improper/Photography/Visual Recording, a felony offense involving moral turpitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order requested interim suspension while a formal disciplinary proceeding is conducted, predicated on the felony conviction; conduct occurring prior to May 3, 2013 is governed by the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20 through 10.1112).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order service and 40-day response requirement (§ 11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail and directed Respondent to file, within forty (40) days, a response containing information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service was by certified mail (receipt numbers provided); the response must specifically address grounds under § 11.25(b)(3) to raise a genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failing to file a response: determination of no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Respondent did not file a response to the Notice and Order, it was determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, and interim suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file the required response supports a finding that no genuine issue of material fact exists for purposes of interim suspension under § 11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended on an interim basis from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO effective the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is interim pending formal disciplinary proceedings and is ordered pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to Administrative Law Judge for formal disciplinary proceeding (§ 11.25(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint is referred to the ALJ for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral initiates the formal adjudicative process where the Respondent will have the opportunity to answer and litigate the Complaint before an ALJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's obligation to file a written answer with the ALJ within 30 days (§ 11.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.36, within thirty (30) days from the date of this Final Order, Respondent's written answer to the Complaint shall be filed with the ALJ and a copy of the answer shall be served on the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the mailing address for service on the OED Director (Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450). Compliance with § 11.36 is mandatory and time-limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish a Notice in the Official Gazette announcing the interim suspension, identifying the respondent and the basis (guilty plea to a felony involving improper photography/visual recording).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice should state the respondent's name, registration number, the suspension, and reference the statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 and 11.59). It also directs readers to the OED FOIA Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to USPTO employees, interested departments/agencies/courts, and state authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to: (1) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (2) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (3) appropriate authorities of any state in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other government entities and relevant state bar authorities are informed of the interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that Respondent comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as part of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 pertains to obligations of a practitioner during suspension (e.g., notice to clients, return of papers/funds); the Order imposes those duties without restating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of Respondent's name from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action severs the respondent's association with electronic accounts and digital credentials used for USPTO filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction remains in effect throughout the interim suspension and until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to prior disciplinary rules for pre-May 3, 2013 conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: For conduct that occurred prior to May 3, 2013, the applicable disciplinary rules are the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20 through 10.1112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes which version of the disciplinary rules governs historical conduct, clarifying which standards apply to alleged prior misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral and further relief clause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint is referred to the ALJ and the Order directs 'such further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order reserves the ability to impose additional remedies or relief as appropriate in the formal proceedings.
